newsitem.title: USA: Boeing offers 737 as military platform.
newsitem.headline: Boeing offers 737 as military platform.

text.p: Boeing Co said Wednesday it is offering its next-generation 737-700 aircraft to the Royal Australian Air Force as an airborne early warning and control system platform.
Boeing is competing with teams led by rivals Lockheed Martin Corp and Raytheon Co for the contract, worth about $390 million for an initial order of at least four aircraft.
The 737 would join Boeing's larger 767 and older 707 jets as a platform for the "eyes in the sky" that allow armed forces to track air and sea targets.
Boeing is joined on the project by British Aerospace Plc and Northrop Grumman Corp, which will provide its 360-degree, multirole electronically scanned array radar.
Australia's project "Wedgetail" is scheduled to go into service in 2002 after an expected contract award in 1999.
